audit_findings.title: Gross cash bridge may capitalize customer float
audit_findings.magnitude: up to $7,127m ($55.58/share; 41.2% of $17,278m base equity value); actual non-surplus portion unquantified
audit_findings.evidence: Therefore, generally we receive cash from the traveler prior to paying our supplier, and this operating cycle represents a working capital source of cash to us.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates that merchant bookings generate operating float and reports $15,426m of deferred merchant bookings plus $2,465m of merchant payables at June 2026. It does not demonstrate that the entire $7,127m cash/STI bridge addition is distributable surplus. Because the addition represents 41.2% of base equity value, an unreconciled float component is material, although the amount improperly included remains unresolved.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile the $7,127m against deferred merchant bookings, merchant payables, restricted traveler deposits, settlement timing and minimum operating liquidity; rerun all scenarios using only demonstrably surplus cash.

audit_findings.title: Consolidated assets and cash flows may not match the parent-share denominator
audit_findings.magnitude: $1,262m filed noncontrolling interest ($9.84/share; 7.3% of base equity value); actual valuation mismatch unquantified
audit_findings.evidence: As of December 31, 2025 and 2024, our ownership interest in trivago was approximately 59.2 % and 59.5 %.
audit_findings.explanation: The consolidated statements demonstrably include trivago while Expedia owns only 59.2%, and the June 2026 balance sheet reports a $1,262m noncontrolling interest. The supplied valuation has no stated perimeter or visible noncontrolling-interest deduction. However, the record does not map the OE worksheet and bridge components sufficiently to establish how much minority value was actually included, so the existence of a material valuation error remains unresolved.
audit_findings.action: Trace net income, D&A, maintenance capex, cash, investments and other bridge assets by entity; either use parent-attributable amounts throughout or value the consolidated business and deduct the minority claim at an appropriate value.

audit_findings.title: Disputed legacy tax claims may be an omitted senior claim
audit_findings.magnitude: $988m-$1,224m of filed proposed federal tax adjustments, subject to interest ($7.71-$9.55/share), before deducting any applicable reserves
audit_findings.evidence: The 2014 to 2016 adjustments would result in federal income tax of approximately $ 431 million, subject to interest.
audit_findings.explanation: The latest filing replaces the earlier adjustments with proposed claims totaling $988m-$1,224m for 2011-2018, plus interest. That is 5.7%-7.1% of base equity value before interest. The company reported $290m of gross unrecognized tax benefits and $133m of accrued interest and penalties at December 2025, but the record does not establish which amounts cover these disputes. The gross claim is therefore demonstrably large, while the unrecorded exposure remains unresolved.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile each IRS adjustment to the latest uncertain-tax-position liability and accrued interest, determine payment timing and defensible probabilities, then deduct and scenario-test only the exposure not already reflected in OE or balance-sheet liabilities.

audit_findings.title: The latest-actual anchor may perpetuate a settlement charge
audit_findings.magnitude: $178m filed 2025 pre-tax settlement charge, equal nominally to 27.2% of the $654.3m OE anchor before tax and OE adjustments
audit_findings.evidence: Legal reserves, occupancy tax and other for the year ended December 31, 2025 primarily included $178 million related to an Italian withholding tax settlement.
audit_findings.explanation: The $178m historical Italian settlement is filed and large relative to the sole-year anchor. If retained and projected as an annual burden, it materially understates normalized OE; if removed without recognizing subsequent-year withholding-tax exposure, value could be overstated. The worksheet treatment is not supplied, so this is a potentially material normalization issue rather than a demonstrated valuation error.
audit_findings.action: Trace the $178m through the 2025 OE calculation; separate the settled 2017-2023 amount from recurring compliance costs and subsequent-year exposure, then rerun the anchor and all scenarios with the supported normalization.

audit_findings.title: Temporary convertible-note accounting expense may be embedded permanently
audit_findings.magnitude: $62m filed 2025 discount amortization; computed upper-bound base effect of approximately $871m or $6.79/share if the full pre-tax amount were restored dollar-for-dollar to OE
audit_findings.evidence: Interest expense increased in 2025 compared to 2024 primarily due to the amortization of the debt discount related to our Convertible Notes due February 2026 as discussed in NOTE 7 — Debt in the notes to the consolidated financial statements.
audit_findings.explanation: The $62m discount amortization was temporary and the notes were cash-settled in February 2026. Using the base DCF's linear capitalization factor, even the conservative upper bound of treating all $62m as after-tax OE changes base value by about 5.0%, from $134.75 to $141.54 per share, still $156.50 below the $298.04 market price. It therefore cannot change the valuation conclusion on the supplied numbers, although correcting it would improve precision.
audit_findings.action: Confirm whether the $62m was retained in OE and, if so, remove it as nonrecurring while verifying that the $1.1bn settlement, including the $78m premium, is already reflected in June 2026 cash and liabilities.

audit_findings.title: Restructuring requires explicit normalization rather than blanket treatment
audit_findings.magnitude: $107m filed 2025 charge; $69m recognized in first-half 2026 plus $35m additional expected
audit_findings.evidence: Based on current plans which are subject to change, we expect approximately $60 million in additional reorganization charges with the majority occurring in the first quarter of 2026.
audit_findings.explanation: The finite restructuring program is large relative to the $654.3m single-year anchor. Perpetuating the $107m 2025 charge understates ongoing OE, while removing it without recognizing the filed 2026 costs overstates near-term value. The latest record also shows that restructuring continued beyond the original estimate, so neither blanket retention nor blanket exclusion is supported.
audit_findings.action: Trace the 2025 charge through OE, distinguish cash severance and benefits from stock compensation, include the filed 2026 program costs at their appropriate timing, and rerun without carrying the temporary program into the terminal period.

audit_findings.title: Unidentified D&A is conservatively left in owner earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: FY2020 residual $175m; residual affecting the 2025 anchor unquantified
audit_findings.evidence: identified eligible D&A is below the filed composite; residual is conservatively left as an expense, not added back: FY2020 $175.0m (16.4% of filed D&A)
audit_findings.explanation: Leaving unidentified D&A as an expense is conservative and cannot itself overstate value. The only supplied amount is the $175m FY2020 residual, while the valuation is anchored to 2025 rather than 2020. The record therefore cannot establish the magnitude or materiality of any understatement in the operative anchor, although historical classification could also affect the too-hard assessment.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the filed D&A composition and OE reconciliation for each year, especially 2025; add back only components demonstrated to be non-economic and rerun the anchor and volatility assessment if a supported 2025 amount is material.
